title: SemaphoreSlim and bounded concurrency
description: Limit concurrent operations with SemaphoreSlim to protect shared resources and improve throughput.

data.text: Sometimes you want to allow some parallelism, but not unlimited parallelism. `SemaphoreSlim` acts like a gate: only a fixed number of threads can pass through at once. This is essential when calling external services with rate limits or when saturating a database connection pool.

A `SemaphoreSlim` is initialized with a count representing available slots. Threads call `Wait` (or `WaitAsync`) to acquire a slot. When they finish, they call `Release` to return the slot. If no slots are available, callers wait until another thread releases one.

data.title: Bounding concurrent HTTP calls

items: **External rate limits** — APIs often cap requests per second. A semaphore enforces the limit without manual throttling.
**Database connection pools** — Connection pools have a fixed size. Bounding prevents exhaustion and connection timeouts.
**File or network I/O** — Opening too many files or sockets at once can overwhelm the OS.

data.title: Always release in a finally block
data.text: If an exception occurs between `WaitAsync` and `Release`, the semaphore slot is lost permanently unless you release in `finally`. This silently reduces the maximum concurrency and can cause starvation.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: SemaphoreSlim limits the number of concurrent operations.
Use it to respect external rate limits and protect finite resources.
Always release the semaphore in a `finally` block.
